package_info.why_malicious: The package was compromised after a new maintainer injected a malicious dependency (flatmap-stream@0.1.1) containing obfuscated code designed to steal cryptocurrency wallet secrets from applications using the Copay wallet library. The code exfiltrates sensitive data to an external server.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when specific Copay-related code paths are executed)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Decodes and decrypts obfuscated payloads using AES256, with the decryption key derived from the package description. This is used to hide the true intent and content of the malicious code.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Obfuscated code and dynamic decryption at runtime are classic indicators of malicious intent, especially when the decryption key is derived from package metadata.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not decrypt and execute hidden payloads at runtime, especially using package metadata as a key.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some legitimate software may use runtime decryption for DRM or licensing, but not in open-source libraries.
key_indicators: Use of package metadata as a cryptographic key

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when wallet file is accessed in Copay context)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Exfiltrates stolen wallet data by sending it via HTTP POST to a remote server (copayapi.host or 111.90.151.134:8080).

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Sending sensitive data to an external server is a hallmark of data exfiltration malware.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A legitimate package should not transmit user data to unknown external servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate telemetry or crash reporting, but only with user consent and to trusted endpoints.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Encrypts stolen data in 200-byte chunks using a public key, then sends it to two hardcoded endpoints (copayapi.host and 111.90.151.134).

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Chunked encryption and exfiltration to multiple endpoints is a strong indicator of targeted data theft.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages do not encrypt and exfiltrate user data to hardcoded, untrusted endpoints.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Secure messaging or backup tools may encrypt and transmit data, but with user awareness and trusted endpoints.

attack_chain.action: Malicious flatmap-stream dependency is loaded as part of event-stream package installation.
attack_chain.leads_to: Obfuscated payload is decrypted and prepared for execution.

attack_chain.action: Malicious code monitors for Copay wallet usage and accesses wallet files.
attack_chain.leads_to: Sensitive wallet data is collected for exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: Collected wallet data is encrypted in chunks using a public key.
attack_chain.leads_to: Data is prepared for secure exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: Encrypted data is exfiltrated via HTTP POST to hardcoded external servers.

behavioral_signatures: Obfuscated or encrypted payloads decrypted at runtime
Dynamic require or crypto usage with package metadata as key
Unexpected network requests to hardcoded external endpoints
Chunked encryption and exfiltration of local files
file_indicators: Presence of flatmap-stream@0.1.1 as a dependency
Obfuscated hex strings and crypto usage in node_modules/flatmap-stream/index.js
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for the presence of flatmap-stream@0.1.1 in the dependency tree, and scan for obfuscated or encrypted payloads in JavaScript files. Flag any runtime decryption of code or use of package metadata as a cryptographic key. Detect outbound HTTP POST requests to copayapi.host or 111.90.151.134, especially if the payload is encrypted or chunked. Alert on any unexpected network activity from build or runtime environments involving these indicators.
